## REQ-PAG-001

**Fields of the PaginationRequest DataSet**

The Payload of a PaginationRequest DataSetMessage contains the mandatory fields PerPage (UInt32 > 0, maximum number of resource DataSetMessages per NetworkMessage of the answer) and Page (UInt32, the requested page); no other field.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: requester
- Condition: The Get carries a PaginationRequest.
- Refs: MG 8.3.11.1, SF-063
- Verification: schema, d7-validate
- Status: draft
- Inventory: MG-8.3.11.1-79ee4a24, MG-8.3.11.1-83b892c6, MG-8.3.11.1-8cb5f159

> The value of PerPage must be > 0.
> — MG 8.3.11.1

## REQ-PAG-002

**A PaginationRequest is answered page by page**

A Get with a PaginationRequest is answered with NetworkMessages that contain at most PerPage resource DataSetMessages each: with Page > 0 only the requested page is published, with Page 0 all pages are published one after the other. A requested page beyond the last page is answered with a page without resource DataSetMessages (proposal SF-063).

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: requester, responder
- Condition: The Get carries a PaginationRequest.
- Refs: MG 8.3.11.1, SF-063
- Verification: d7-test
- Status: draft
- Inventory: MG-8.3.11.1-35d839fd, MG-8.3.11.1-6175a9d6, MG-8.3.11.1-c4df177f, MG-8.3.11.1-cd18f8ad

> A published message to the topic method Get may use PerPage to announce, how many DataSetMessages it expects maximum in the related publication.
> — MG 8.3.11.1

> If several NetworkMessages must be published to transport the relevant DataSetMessages, the value of Page shows which page is requested.
> — MG 8.3.11.1

> The value of Page must be > 0 to get a defined page with related information.
> — MG 8.3.11.1

Notes: "may use PerPage" refers to the use of the PaginationRequest as a whole; PerPage itself is Mandatory (SF-063).

## REQ-PAG-003

**Fields of the Pagination DataSet**

The Payload of a Pagination DataSetMessage contains the mandatory fields TotalCount (UInt32), PerPage (UInt32), Page (UInt32), HasNext (Boolean) and PaginationId (String in the form of a MessageId); no other field.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: publisher
- Condition: The publication carries a Pagination.
- Refs: MG 8.3.11.2, SF-063
- Verification: schema, d7-validate
- Status: draft
- Inventory: MG-8.3.11.2-01941170, MG-8.3.11.2-4e072fbd, MG-8.3.11.2-8e50e6a3, MG-8.3.11.2-97e960a0, MG-8.3.11.2-bceb2d3b

## REQ-PAG-004

**Pagination values are consistent**

In a Pagination, TotalCount is the number of resource DataSetMessages of the whole series (helper DataSets not counted), PerPage the maximum number of resource DataSetMessages per NetworkMessage (the requested PerPage when answering a PaginationRequest), Page the number of the published page starting at 1, HasNext true exactly if Page · PerPage &lt; TotalCount, and PaginationId the MessageId of the first NetworkMessage of the series; a NetworkMessage contains at most PerPage resource DataSetMessages (proposal SF-063).

- Keyword: MUST (implicit, SF-035)
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: publisher
- Condition: The publication carries a Pagination.
- Refs: MG 8.3.11.2, SF-035, SF-063
- Verification: d7-validate, d7-monitor
- Status: draft
- Inventory: MG-8.3.11.2-1b7ec9ae, MG-8.3.11.2-2d5655ce, MG-8.3.11.2-35875bdf, MG-8.3.11.2-42fdc31a, MG-8.3.11.2-e61bb795, MG-8.3.11.2-f0bcbef0

> A published message to the topic methods Pub might use TotalCount to announce, how many of the actual processed resources can be expected.
> — MG 8.3.11.2

> A published message to the topic methods Pub may use PerPage to announce, how many of the TotalCount DataSetMessages will be included in this publication.
> — MG 8.3.11.2

> HasNext shows if an additional NetworkMessage can be expected.
> — MG 8.3.11.2

> The PaginationId contains the &lt;MessageId> of the first/initial paginated NetworkMessage in this series.
> — MG 8.3.11.2

Notes: Within one NetworkMessage the payload checker verifies the field types, Page ≥ 1, the number of resource DataSetMessages ≤ PerPage, HasNext and – on Page 1 – PaginationId = MessageId; the order of a series is checked by D7 (monitor).

## REQ-PAG-005

**Too many DataSetMessages are paginated**

A publisher that has more resource DataSetMessages than fit into one NetworkMessage (by its own limit or by the PerPage of a PaginationRequest) publishes them in several NetworkMessages to the same topic, each with a Pagination, until all DataSetMessages are published. This applies to every resource with a list of DataSetMessages (e.g. MAM, Health, Profile, PublicationList, ReferenceDesignation).

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: publisher
- Refs: MG 8.3.11, MG 9.1.1, MG 9.1.2, MG 9.1.7, MG 9.1.8, MG 9.1.10, SF-063
- Verification: d7-monitor, d7-test
- Status: draft
- Inventory: MG-8.3.11-0a2549a0, MG-8.3.11-135129ca, MG-9.1.1-5f90ef30, MG-9.1.1-a242a498, MG-9.1.10-23d0ef72, MG-9.1.10-e685d6ba, MG-9.1.2-0af27f74, MG-9.1.2-262fa218, MG-9.1.7-a9a20bff, MG-9.1.7-fe765cc6, MG-9.1.8-03c98043, MG-9.1.8-ea9cd5b6

> To prevent this, an optional DataSetMessage with Pagination information is available to indicate that there are other NetworkMessages with associated DataSetMessages.
> — MG 8.3.11

> Once too many DataSetMessages are available to add to a single NetworkMessage, pagination mechanism must be used (8.3.11 Pagination).
> — MG 9.1.1

> The publisher must publish as many NetworkMessages to the same topic, using pagination object for telling so, till all DataSetMessages are published.
> — MG 9.1.1

Notes: For publications not triggered by a Get the publisher defines the maximum size on its own (MG 8.3.11). The pagination sentences of the other resources (Data, Event, SubscriptionList, …) are mapped in C-028.

## REQ-PAG-006

**A subscriber re-triggers a too long publication with PaginationRequest**

An application that cannot handle the size of a publication requests the information again via Get with a PaginationRequest.

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: subscriber, requester
- Condition: A received publication is too long for the application.
- Refs: MG 8.3.11
- Verification: manual
- Status: draft
- Inventory: MG-8.3.11-7898fea4

> If these messages are too long for a specific application, that application must re-trigger publication of the information by using PaginationRequest.
> — MG 8.3.11

## REQ-PAG-007

**Paginated DataSetMessages are consistent**

If NetworkMessages are paginated, the publisher fetches the provided DataSetMessages so that the series is consistent (e.g. a snapshot taken at the start of the series).

- Keyword: MUST
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: publisher
- Condition: The publication is paginated.
- Refs: MG 8.3.11
- Verification: manual
- Status: draft
- Inventory: MG-8.3.11-19ff609c

## REQ-PAG-008

**PaginationRequest only in Get, Pagination only in Pub**

A NetworkMessage contains a PaginationRequest only with the method Get and a Pagination only with the method Pub, each at most once (proposal SF-062 (b)).

- Keyword: MUST (implicit, SF-035)
- Levels: L1 MUST · L2 MUST · L3 MUST
- Domain: messaging · Applies to: publisher, requester, responder
- Refs: MG 8.3.11, MG 8.3.11.1, MG 8.3.11.2, SF-035, SF-062
- Verification: schema, d7-validate
- Status: draft
- Inventory: MG-8.3.11-083cc809, MG-8.3.11-1bd35c16

> The Pagination object and PaginationRequest object differ for the methods Pub and Get.
> — MG 8.3.11

> A subscriber that wants to request information via …/Get/&lt;Resource> can add a PaginationRequest object to its payload to define the maximum number of DataSetMessages the NetworkMessage may contain so that the subscriber is able to handle it.
> — MG 8.3.11

Notes: "Pagination information can be used … for every Method" (MG 8.3.11) contradicts the method-specific definitions of 8.3.11.1 (Get) and 8.3.11.2 (Pub); a receiver ignores a misplaced helper (REQ-MSG-046).
